column1: # jobleft skill taxonomy: skills in tech and non-tech work, the words postings and profiles use for them, and which
# skills can stand in for each other.
# Source: written new for jobleft by the match lane (2026-09-25). First-party data; no third-party list was copied.
# Licence: same as the jobleft project. Skill names are ordinary names of tools, methods and trade skills.
# Format: id | name | kind | families | aliases | related skills
#   * kind: lang (programming language), tool, skill, method, regime (a rule set a job is subject to, such as HIPAA;
#     it counts only when a requirement list names it), spoken (a human language).
#   * families: the kinds of work (data/occupations.tsv) where the skill belongs. Macros: @tech @health @office
#     @trades @edu @mgmt, and * for every kind. A skill named only in passing (not in a requirement list) counts
#     only when the job's kind of work is one of these.
#   * aliases: the words for the skill. Matching is on whole words, longest first, so "JavaScript" is never "Java"
#     and "C++" is never "C". A leading = means the letters must match in case ("Go", "R", "Excel").
#     A trailing @ctx needs context in the text around it (see CONTEXT_RULES in src/taxonomy.ts).
#   * related: skills that can stand in for this one (half credit, and the skill still shows as missing).
#     Pairs are symmetric. Names that look alike are never related (Java and JavaScript, C and C++).
